answer: Decaying capacity quotas price out sybils by measuring how much copper an operator locks into a liquidity-lineage knoll before any agent starts a routing voyage. Every voyage consumes decaying bandwidth credits that must be repurchased each epoch, and because the knoll traces capital provenance to shared funding origins, all clones financed by the same treasury tally together while an honest newcomer starts at one. The protocol charges $N^2$ units of copper per voyage for the $N$-th linked clone, forcing a sybil operator to pay quadratically rising capital or mixing fees to sever provenance.
